Operational_Support_Criterion: Clinical information can be associated with the Care Encounter in which it was documented; Care Encounters can be chronologically ordered; associated Medical Record Entries can be identified or retrieved; the view does not require a duplicate authoritative clinical record.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic patient medical record contains Medical Record Entries distributed across multiple dated Care Encounters, allowing chronological grouping to be exercised.
Common_Information_Model: Care Encounter (Contact) provides the chronological care-event dimension; Medical Record Entries retain their clinical content and are associated with Care Encounter context.
FOLDER_Representation: Care Encounter-oriented FOLDER nodes can index references to the existing clinical objects associated with each Care Encounter.
LINK_Representation: Explicit LINK relationships can associate the Care Encounter COMPOSITION with corresponding clinical COMPOSITIONs; retrieval may require relationship traversal and target resolution.
CLUSTER_Representation: Archetyped relationship metadata can represent the Care Encounter association in the relevant clinical context and expose it through governed paths.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Demonstrates derivability of a chronological Care Encounter view. Does not demonstrate an implemented UI, retrieval performance, or clinical usability.

Functional_Requirement: Episode-oriented retrieval for a selected Health Problem
Operational_Support_Criterion: An Episode of Care represents a distinct Health Problem; clinical information can be associated with that Episode across multiple Care Encounters; associated Medical Record Entries can be identified or retrieved without creating an Episode-specific duplicate authoritative record.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic patient medical record includes acute and chronic Health Problems represented across one or more Care Encounters, allowing longitudinal Episode-oriented reconstruction to be exercised.
Common_Information_Model: Episode of Care provides the longitudinal Health Problem dimension and remains distinct from Care Encounter; clinical statements remain in their source ENTRYs and COMPOSITIONs.
FOLDER_Representation: Episode-oriented FOLDER nodes can index references to existing EHR objects associated with the selected Episode of Care.
LINK_Representation: LINKs can associate clinical ENTRYs with Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs, including primary and additional associated Episode relationships according to the evaluated design.
CLUSTER_Representation: Repeating archetyped Episode references associate each referenced Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION with a constrained relationship role (Primary or Associated). The additional model-level invariant requiring exactly one Primary Episode association per clinical ENTRY is not independently enforced by the archetype.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Demonstrates representational capability for longitudinal Episode reconstruction. Does not demonstrate cross-repository retrieval, query performance, or a production Episode-oriented UI.

Operational_Support_Criterion: Medical Record Entries can be classified by Clinical Section independently of Care Encounter and Episode organization; information belonging to a selected section can be identified or retrieved without duplicating clinical content.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic patient medical record assigns Medical Record Entries to Clinical Sections, allowing section-oriented organization of the same longitudinal clinical content.
Common_Information_Model: Clinical Section is an independent semantic classification dimension of Medical Record Entries.
FOLDER_Representation: Clinical Section-oriented FOLDER nodes can provide a patient-level index over existing clinical objects classified to the relevant section.
LINK_Representation: Clinical Section remains part of the common information model; LINK supplies relationship traversal while section classification is retained with the clinical information or associated classification.
CLUSTER_Representation: Clinical Section classification can be represented as governed relationship/context metadata and queried through stable archetyped paths.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Design-level section classification and section-oriented views are representable. The technical PoC did not validate a complete Clinical Section retrieval/view workflow across all patterns; Clinical Section FOLDER-to-ENTRY retrieval (R03) was explicitly out of scope. No implemented UI, terminology completeness, or usability is demonstrated.

Functional_Requirement: Combined Clinical Section × Care Encounter/Episode views
Operational_Support_Criterion: Clinical Section classification can coexist with Care Encounter and Episode associations; the same Medical Record Entry retains the context required for these dimensions; combined selections can be constructed without context-specific copies of clinical statements.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic patient medical record combines Clinical Section assignments with Care Encounter and Episode/Health Problem context for the same Medical Record Entries.
Common_Information_Model: Care Encounter, Episode of Care, and Clinical Section are distinct but combinable dimensions over the same underlying clinical information.
Common_Supporting_Model_Evidence: local/JPM - Contact - Care Encounter.t.json; local/JPM - Episode of care.t.json; local/openEHR-EHR-SECTION.adhoc.v1.adl; local/openEHR-EHR-SECTION.soap.v0.adl
FOLDER_Representation: Multiple directory/index organizations can provide Care Encounter-, Episode-, and Clinical Section-oriented access to references to the same underlying EHR content.
LINK_Representation: Explicit Care Encounter and Episode relationships can be traversed while Clinical Section classification is retained independently, allowing combined application/query projections.
CLUSTER_Representation: Governed relationship metadata can expose Care Encounter reference, Episode associations, and Clinical Section classification together for filtering and projection.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Combined Clinical Section × Care Encounter/Episode views are conceptually derivable without clinical-data duplication. The technical PoC did not execute and validate complete combined section/context retrieval workflows for all three patterns; illustrative combined AQL examples are not executed-test evidence. No combined-filter performance or UI is demonstrated.

Operational_Support_Criterion: Two distinct linear views can be derived from identifiable patient Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs: a Diagnosis List filtered by Classification = Diagnosis and a Problem List filtered by Classification = Problem; the Classification attribute is accessible on each Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION; neither view requires a separately maintained authoritative copy of Episode clinical content.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic longitudinal patient history includes multiple Health Problem/Episode trajectories serving as source objects for the two classification-filtered views; the dataset alone does not prove execution of both complete list queries.
Common_Information_Model: Each Episode of Care is represented by an identifiable Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION with an accessible Classification attribute (Diagnosis or Problem). Diagnosis List and Problem List are two distinct derived linear views over those COMPOSITIONs, not separately persisted authoritative lists.
FOLDER_Representation: Episode-oriented FOLDER references can support navigation to existing Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs; Diagnosis and Problem views are derived by filtering the referenced or retrieved Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs by Classification, not by treating FOLDER organization itself as the list.
LINK_Representation: Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs remain identifiable and classification-bearing objects. LINK relationships associate clinical information with Episodes but do not constitute the two linear lists; the lists are derived by filtering Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs by Classification.
CLUSTER_Representation: Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs supply the classification-bearing longitudinal objects; CLUSTER metadata governs clinical-to-Episode relationships but does not replace Classification-based selection of the two linear lists.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Supports design-level derivability of separate Diagnosis and Problem views from Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs using Classification. The technical PoC did not establish that both complete classification-filtered lists were generated and validated. No ordering, presentation, or clinical usability was tested.

Operational_Support_Criterion: A separate persistent clinician-curated hierarchical Diagnosis and Problem List COMPOSITION can explicitly represent grouping, ordering and/or parent-child relationships and reference identifiable Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs; the hierarchy can be revised without duplicating or replacing the authoritative clinical content of referenced Episodes; it remains distinct from the two derived linear views in US5.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic scenario provides Episode-of-Care source objects that could be referenced by a curated hierarchy; the dataset itself does not establish a fully populated or technically validated hierarchical-list COMPOSITION.
Common_Information_Model: A distinct hierarchical Diagnosis and Problem List COMPOSITION persists the clinician-curated organization and references to existing Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs. This organizational COMPOSITION is not the same as a FOLDER directory or the LINK/CLUSTER patterns used to relate clinical entries to Episodes.
Common_Supporting_Model_Evidence: local/JPM - Master diagnosis and problem list MENTORING.t.json; local/JPM - Contextual diagnosis and problem list MENTORING.t.json; local/openEHR-EHR-CLUSTER.problem_links.v1.adl
FOLDER_Representation: The separate hierarchical-list COMPOSITION contains the curated hierarchy and references to Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs. FOLDER-based organization may additionally index the Episodes, but a FOLDER tree is not itself the required hierarchical-list COMPOSITION.
LINK_Representation: The separate hierarchical-list COMPOSITION documents the curated hierarchy and references Episode-of-Care COMPOSITIONs. LINK-based clinical-to-Episode relationships remain an independent implementation pattern; LINK traversal alone does not demonstrate the curated list.
CLUSTER_Representation: The separate hierarchical-list COMPOSITION represents curated hierarchy and Episode-of-Care COMPOSITION references using its own clinical modelling structures; the CLUSTER-based clinical-to-Episode association pattern does not by itself constitute this hierarchical list.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Design-level representability of a separate clinician-curated hierarchical-list COMPOSITION and its references is assessed; the technical PoC did not implement or validate this complete COMPOSITION and hierarchy for all three patterns. No editing workflow, collaborative curation, conflict resolution, UI usability, or clinical validation is demonstrated.

Functional_Requirement: SOAP-oriented documentation for one or more Health Problems
Operational_Support_Criterion: A complete SOAP progress note is one indivisible clinical documentation unit, represented technically by four OBSERVATION.progress_note.v1 ENTRYs under SECTION.soap.v0 (Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan). The note has one coherent Episode-of-Care assignment, potentially including Primary and Associated Episodes; the four technical ENTRYs must not be treated as independently assignable clinical SOAP notes. Views do not require duplicate authoritative clinical content.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic longitudinal scenario includes progress documentation and multiple Health Problem contexts suitable for exercising SOAP-oriented documentation and Episode associations.
Common_Information_Model: SECTION.soap.v0 structures a single clinical SOAP note using four technical OBSERVATION.progress_note.v1 ENTRYs. Episode associations apply coherently to the clinical note despite technical ENTRY granularity; the four ENTRYs do not represent four independent clinical documentation units.
Common_Supporting_Model_Evidence: local/JPM - SOAP initial encounter .t.json; local/JPM - SOAP progress note.t.json; local/openEHR-EHR-SECTION.soap.v0.adl
FOLDER_Representation: FOLDER-based Episode/navigation structures can reference the clinical documentation participating in SOAP-oriented and Health Problem-oriented views; SOAP structure remains represented in the clinical documentation model.
LINK_Representation: LINK relationships can encode Episode associations at technical ENTRY level, but all four ENTRYs constituting one SOAP note must preserve the same clinical Episode assignment; technical relationship multiplicity must not be confused with separate SOAP notes.
CLUSTER_Representation: Relationship CLUSTERs may be present at ENTRY.protocol for the four technical SOAP ENTRYs; their Episode references and Primary/Associated roles must be coherent for the one clinical SOAP note. Exactly one Primary association per clinical unit is a model-level invariant, not independently enforced by the archetype.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: SOAP reconstruction through SECTION structures and Episode associations is supported by selected PoC tests. MR4 and MR8 each form one clinical SOAP note despite four technical OBSERVATION.progress_note.v1 ENTRYs; expanded ENTRY-level relationship counts do not imply independently assigned clinical notes. No full clinical documentation workflow, UI, decision support, or usability validation is demonstrated.

Operational_Support_Criterion: Information required for dashboard projections can be identified through Clinical Section classification; relevant Medical Record Entries can be retrieved or selected; widgets/views can be constructed as query/application projections without a separate authoritative dashboard-specific copy.
Dataset_Evidence: The synthetic patient medical record contains Clinical Section assignments across longitudinal Medical Record Entries, providing the source information required for section-oriented projections.
Common_Information_Model: Clinical Section is an independent classification dimension that can be projected across the longitudinal record and combined with Care Encounter or Episode context.
FOLDER_Representation: Clinical Section-oriented directory/index structures can support navigation to existing EHR content used by dashboard projections.
LINK_Representation: LINK relationships preserve access to relevant contextual objects while Clinical Section classification supplies the selection dimension used by application-level dashboard projections.
CLUSTER_Representation: Clinical Section and relationship metadata can be exposed through stable archetyped paths for query/application projection into section-oriented dashboard views.
Evaluation_Result: Supported at design level by FOLDER, LINK, and CLUSTER
Evidence_Boundary: Demonstrates availability of information needed for section-oriented projections. Does not demonstrate an implemented dashboard, visualization quality, interaction design, response time, usability, or clinical effectiveness.
